newsitem.title: UK: London gold, silver weak but off day's lows.
newsitem.headline: London gold, silver weak but off day's lows.

text.p: Gold and silver drifted in lower ranges on Friday afternoon following overnight losses which analysts said may herald the resumption of a recent downtrend.
"The general feeling is cautiously bearish," a dealer said. Bullion fixed slightly firmer at $380.00 an ounce, compared to $379.60 in the morning and a London close of $380.20/$380.70.
Silver was also off its overnight lows of $4.85 an ounce, but it was still two cents down from Thursday's close at $4.90/$4.92 an ounce.
Analysts said technical price charts indicated gold and silver may have finished their recent upward correction and were set to revisit recent lows.
"The medium-term paths for both gold and silver are clearly down," said technical analyst Cliff Green of Trend Analysis. The market's recent correction higher appeared over, he added.
"The precious metals, having corrected their oversold conditions, could see further selling pressure now," technical analyst Elli Gifford of Investment Research of Cambridge said in a commentary.
Gold was expected to meet strong resistance at $381 after recent losses, while silver's roof was at $5.00, analysts said.
Some dealers said gold's $380 level may hold until after the end-of-month expiry of options, which give the right but not the obligation to buy or sell metal at a given price.
In the longer term gold was targetting $375 and then $373 an ounce, while silver was at risk of heading to the $4.60 area - unseen for 18 months -- in the next few weeks, Green said.
"They will probably test recent lows in the near term but will also be vulnerable to breaking these," Green said of gold and silver. "I'm quite negative in the medium term.
Analysts said that although New York silver stocks had been falling in recent weeks, givng bullish signals to the market, physical silver stocks in London were very high.
"Storage space is at a premium," one analyst said.
Palladium gained $1.00 from Thursday's London close and was trading at $116.00/$117.00.
It had fixed at a 3-1/2 year low of $115.25 in the morning and was vulnerable to further downward pressure.
"The (platinum group metals) are restless, but there's no sense of direction at this point," a dealer said.
